documents.title: Machine_5 Compressor — Operating Manual
documents.content: Machine_5 is a Rotary Screw Air Compressor located in Zone C - Bay 1. Normal operating ranges: Temperature 65–90°C (oil temperature, optimal 75–80°C), Vibration 0.10–0.22 mm/s, RPM 3000–3800 (optimal 3400), Power Consumption 950–1300 W. Compressor type: Rotary screw, oil-injected. Motor rating: 1.5 kW. Free Air Delivery (FAD): 200 L/min at 8 bar. Maximum working pressure: 10 bar. Oil capacity: 4 liters. Oil type: Compressor oil ISO VG 100. Air receiver capacity: 50 liters. Inlet filter type: Dry panel filter. Startup procedure: (1) Check oil level — must be visible in sight glass, (2) Check air receiver drain valve is closed, (3) Verify outlet valve is open, (4) Start motor — compressor will load automatically when pressure drops below setpoint, (5) Allow to reach operating pressure (8 bar) before using compressed air. Shutdown procedure: (1) Press stop button — compressor will unload before stopping, (2) Open air receiver drain valve to release condensate — open for 30 seconds, (3) Close drain valve, (4) For extended shutdown, open receiver drain valve fully.

documents.title: Machine_5 Compressor — Maintenance Schedule
documents.content: Machine_5 Compressor Preventive Maintenance Schedule. DAILY: Check oil level in sight glass — must be between MIN and MAX. Drain condensate from air receiver — open drain valve for 30 seconds. Check operating pressure is at 8 bar setpoint. Listen for unusual knocking or squealing. Check oil cooler is clean and air can flow through freely. EVERY 100 HOURS: Clean or replace air inlet filter element — hold up to light to check blockage. Check oil for discoloration or milky appearance (indicates water contamination). Inspect oil cooler fins for dirt blockage — clean with compressed air. Check all hose connections for leaks using soapy water. EVERY 500 HOURS (approx 3 months): Replace compressor oil. Replace oil filter element. Replace air filter element regardless of appearance. Check safety valve operation — pull ring to verify it releases. Inspect drive belt for cracking or wear — replace if cracks visible. EVERY 1000 HOURS (approx 6 months): Replace oil separator element. Inspect and clean check valve. Inspect pressure relief valve. Clean entire oil cooler with degreaser. Check motor bearing temperature and lubrication. EVERY 2000 HOURS (ANNUALLY): Full service by qualified technician. Replace all wear parts including screw element tip seals. Motor overhaul inspection. Pressure vessel inspection certification. Replace all hoses.

documents.title: Machine_5 Compressor — Alert Explanations
documents.content: Machine_5 Compressor Alert Guide. HIGH TEMPERATURE ALERT (Warning >90°C, Critical >105°C — auto shutdown): Compressor overheating is the most common fault. Causes: blocked oil cooler (most common), low oil level, failed cooling fan, high ambient temperature (above 40°C), blocked inlet filter restricting airflow, worn screw element. Actions at Warning: Clean oil cooler immediately — use compressed air to blow through fins. Check oil level. Ensure room ventilation is adequate. At Critical: Compressor will auto-shutdown on thermal overload — do not restart until cooled and fault identified. OIL CARRYOVER (oil in air lines): Indicates oil separator element saturated (replace at 1000 hours), oil level too high, wrong oil type used, or compressor operating at low pressure. Actions: Replace oil separator element. Reduce oil level to MAX mark. HIGH VIBRATION ALERT (Warning >0.3 mm/s, Critical >0.5 mm/s): Causes include worn screw element bearings, loose drive belt, motor bearing failure, compressor mounted on uneven surface, foreign object in air inlet. Actions: Check belt tension immediately. Verify mounting bolts are tight. If vibration accompanied by knocking noise, stop immediately — risk of screw element seizure. PRESSURE NOT REACHING SETPOINT: Causes include inlet filter blocked (most common), air leak in system, worn screw element, pressure switch fault, high demand exceeding FAD. Actions: Check and replace inlet filter first. POWER CONSUMPTION HIGH (Warning >1500 W, Critical >1800 W): High power consumption with low output pressure is the classic sign of valve leakage or worn screw element. Actions: Check for air leaks at all connections. Schedule screw element inspection.

documents.title: Machine_5 Compressor — Operator Guidelines
documents.content: Machine_5 Compressor Operator Guidelines. SAFETY RULES: Never remove pressure vessel inspection covers under pressure — always depressurize first. Never exceed maximum working pressure of 10 bar. Ensure safety valve is not tampered with or blocked — it is the last line of defense against over-pressure. Do not use compressed air to clean clothing or skin — serious injury can result. Always wear ear protection when working near running compressor — noise level exceeds 85 dB. OPERATING TIPS: Allow compressor to reach operating temperature (75°C) before heavy use. Drain air receiver condensate daily — water in air lines causes corrosion and damages tools. Keep inlet area clear — compressor must draw clean, cool air. Check oil level when compressor is stopped and has been off for 5 minutes. Compressor room temperature must not exceed 40°C — ensure adequate ventilation. COMPRESSED AIR QUALITY: For painting or food applications, use additional air dryer and filter. Check outlet air for oil smell — indicates oil separator needs replacement. FAULT RESET PROCEDURE: After thermal shutdown — allow 15-minute cool down, check and fix fault cause, reset thermal overload button on motor, press compressor start button. Do not reset more than 3 times without investigating cause. SHIFT HANDOVER CHECKLIST: Record operating hours, note oil level (add if needed), drain condensate and note amount, record operating pressure, note any unusual sounds, log any auto-shutdowns during shift, check inlet filter condition.
